items.title: Show HN: Ever Wanted to Call Codex from Claude Code? My Harness Orchestrator
items.why_it_matters: An indie developer shipped `harness-subagent`, an orchestrator that lets you call Codex (or other models) directly from Claude Code. Since you use both Claude Code and Codex, this lets you delegate sub-tasks to Codex without leaving your terminal, saving you high-cost Claude tokens on simpler tasks. Clone the `harness-subagent` repo today and configure your Claude Code to delegate a basic CSS or boilerplate generation task to Codex.

items.title: Claude Pacer: a menu-bar that says if your Claude session will last till reset
items.why_it_matters: A developer built and shipped `claude-pacer`, a Mac menu-bar app that tracks your Claude rate limits and predicts if your session will last until the reset. When you are in a flow state vibe-coding, hitting the Claude rate limit abruptly ruins your momentum. Download the menu bar app from the GitHub repo today so you can pace your coding sessions and avoid getting blocked mid-build.

items.title: Using Claude hosted agents to solve open source bugs and perf improvements
items.why_it_matters: Jaipilot, a tool that uses Claude hosted agents to automatically solve open-source bugs and performance issues, is now available on the GitHub Marketplace. As you learn Git and commit discipline on your AI-ingest repo, you can use automated agents to review your code and suggest PRs for bugs you might have missed. Install the Jaipilot integration on your AI-ingest GitHub repository this week and run it to see if it catches any edge cases in your ingestion logic.

items.title: Contextual News Search APIs: A Deep Comparison for AI, RAG, and Research
items.why_it_matters: A developer published a deep comparison of contextual news search APIs for AI and RAG, detailing costs, latency, and data quality. Because you are currently building AI-ingest to filter news, choosing the right API to feed your app is the difference between clean data and absolute noise. Look at the top-rated free or low-cost API in this comparison and write a quick fetch script in your Next.js backend to test its payload against your current ingestion logic.
